Part 2 — Proposals for approval

P1 · A richer Department card (your item 2)Proposal

Three columns, every figure the Department’s own or added up from it — nothing the hero above already shows. Scholarship students in 2025-26: SC 74.23 lakh and OBC, EBC and DNT 56.47 lakh (Pre + Post-Matric, as the Department’s chart gives them), the 12-year trend of both, and SHREYAS 2,506 scholars, up from 409. Where the fund went: the nine schemes’ shares, the largest four named. Hostels and Top Class Education: the four figures, plus Top Class Schools’ rise from 1,275 to 27,007 placements.

P2 · Two-part donuts become a split bar, and red leaves the chartsProposal

A ring with two slices makes the reader judge angles; a bar with counts and shares reads at once. Red is the colour of an error on this estate, so a category never gets it. Mode-II keeps one colour on every page (it is brown on the landing card and red here today). Applies to SHRESHTA’s two rings and Senior Citizens’ two; SMILE’s three-part gender ring stays a ring but loses red.

P3 · Portal figures in the units the landing page uses, grouped by meaningProposal

“34,85,39,944” becomes 34.85 Cr, as on the landing page; the exact figure stays in the source note and for screen readers. Reach in one row (Total, then Women and Youth as shares of it), engagement in the next. The map legend switches to lakh. The theme chips go where a page has only two themes.

P4 · SMILE funds as one utilisation figureProposal

Released and Utilised stood as two unrelated cards. One card says what the pair means: ₹5.88 Cr of ₹7.25 Cr, 81% utilised.

P4b · SMILE digital delivery as metersProposal

Percentages read as progress on a bar.

P5 · Elderline calls get their totalProposal

The bars broke the calls down but never said how many there were: 2,98,800, the sum of the five kinds, which the landing card already rounds to 2.99 lakh.

P6 · One date formatProposal

The pages mix “As on 05.10.2026”, “up to 30.09.2026”, “As of 07 Oct 2026” and the footer’s “01.10.2026”. Proposal: DD MMM YYYY everywhere (07 Oct 2026), the format the open DBIM branch already adopts.

P7 · Landing card labels in sentence weight, not capitalsProposal

Long indicator names in small capitals wrap to three lines on the Senior Citizens card (“TOTAL NUMBER OF ASSISTIVE DEVICES DISTRIBUTED · RVY”). Capitals stay for short labels; long ones drop to normal case, and every row of figures reserves the same label height so the figures sit on one line (the Department card’s fourth figure sits lower today).

P8 · “Type of Applicant” becomes “Beneficiary Group”Proposal

A citizen reading a dashboard isn’t applying for anything; the filter chooses SC, OBC, EBC or DNT figures.

P9 · DAPSC mandate table says its own answerProposal

Subtitle “M/D wise DAPSC allocation vis a vis Mandated Allocation” becomes “Allocation by each Ministry and Department against its mandated share.” A one-line summary above the table: “5 of 10 meet their mandate.” (counted from the table).

P10 · The Department page stops telling each trend twiceProposal

The summary cards carry small trend lines that the Year by Year Trends section then draws in full. The cards keep their figures; the trends live once, in the section built for them. The cards also come out level.

P11 · Motion, per the Apple guidanceProposal

The theme chips and segmented buttons swap content instantly. A 150 ms cross-fade on the swapped panel (none when the reader asks for reduced motion) keeps the eye on what changed. Buttons already respond on press.
